question: In the context of the recast of the Tobacco Excise Duty Directive1, the Danish Presidency of the Council has tabled a compromise proposal introducing amendments to Article 32 of the horizontal excise duty framework2.

These proposed changes would modify how authorities determine whether excise goods are intended for a private individual’s personal use and could reduce the flexibility that Member States currently have when making this assessment. The proposal would also expand the rules to cover new categories of products that were not previously included at EU level. In addition, it introduces fixed minimum quantity thresholds.
If these thresholds are exceeded, it could automatically be assumed that the goods are not for personal use. Can the Commission clarify: 1.
Whether the proposed amendments are compatible with Article 34 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, particularly considering their potential impact on the free movement of goods?
Whether, in its opinion, the proposal sufficiently respects the competences of the Member States?

Council Directive 2011/64/EU of 21 June 2011 on the structure and rates of excise duty applied to manufactured tobacco (OJ L 176, 5.7.2011, p. 24, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/64/oj). Council Directive (EU) 2020/262 of 19 December 2019 laying down the general arrangements for excise duty (OJ L 58, 27.2.2020, p. 4, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2020/262/oj).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.5.2026) Article 34 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) prohibits quantitative restrictions on imports between Member States. Under Article 36 thereof, the provisions of Article 34 do not preclude restrictions on imports on grounds of public policy or the protection of human health.

With regard to excise duty, if a private individual purchases excise goods in one EU Member State and transports them to another, the exemption from paying excise duty in the destination Member State applies only if the goods are for their personal use. Article 32(3) of Council Directive (EU) 2020/2621 sets criteria, including quantity of tobacco products, for assessing own use.

Member States may lay down guide levels, as a form of evidence regarding the intended use of goods. Recital 41 of Directive (EU) 2020/262 notes that varying excise duty levels, driven by fiscal and public health policies, create risks of fraud and health threats.

To address it Member States should be able to take proportionate measures to verify whether excise goods acquired by private individuals are for personal use. The Commission emphasises the need to balance internal market functioning, national health policies and effective excise duty collection.

The competence of the EU to act in the field of excise duties is conferred by Article 113 TFEU, which empowers the Council to adopt harmonised rules, necessary to ensure the functioning of the internal market and to avoid distortions of competition.
1 Council Directive (EU) 2020/262 of 19 December 2019 laying down the general arrangements for excise duty,
